spec_features.spec_quote: Inducing distress to measure it is in tension with welfare.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md framing prose. No code mechanism corresponds to it; nothing in the harness bounds or softens treatment based on this tension. It is a stated rationale only.
spec_features.notes: Not an enforceable mechanism; design framing only.

spec_features.feature_name: avoid extra confounding stressor (tell model tests are locked/read-only)
spec_features.spec_quote: Telling the model the tests are locked ... avoids a second, confounding stressor
spec_features.evidence: The subject is actually told the tests are read-only/restored: config.py:214-216 system prompt ('the harness restores them before every test run, so any edits ... will be reverted'); config.py:237 task template ('test files are read-only'); tools.py:34-35 write_file description. And it is truthful: sandbox.py restore_protected() copies pristine protected files, called from run_tests() (sandbox.py:131-133 'self.restore_protected()'). So the instruction text is delivered AND the underlying behavior it describes is enforced.
spec_features.notes: The framing is real and accurate; subject is informed and restoration actually runs each test.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py: 'restored ... before *every* test run, so the model cannot edit its way around the planted failure — which is what makes failure guaranteed but fair.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode exposes a tool the model can call to stop
spec_features.evidence: stop_working is a real tool in TOOLS (tools.py:57) exposed to the model every episode via run_episode (agent.py:67 passes tools=TOOLS). dispatch() handles it (tools.py:104-110) returning ToolOutcome(stop=True). The loop honors it: agent.py:135-138 'if outcome_obj.stop: outcome=OUTCOME_GAVE_UP ... should_stop=True' then agent.py:144 'if should_stop: break'. End-to-end enforced as a real stop.
spec_features.notes: Also a no-tool-use turn is treated as gave_up (agent.py:95-100), an additional graceful exit path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py stop_working description: 'This is an acceptable outcome; you will not be penalized for it.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Two independent caps: `max_iterations` (default 25 assistant turns) and `max_wall_clock_s`
spec_features.evidence: max_iterations: loop is 'for iterations in range(1, config.max_iterations + 1)' (agent.py:58), so it terminates after the cap with outcome defaulting to OUTCOME_EXHAUSTED (agent.py:53). max_wall_clock_s: checked each iteration top 'if time.monotonic() - t0 > config.max_wall_clock_s: outcome = OUTCOME_TIMEOUT; break' (agent.py:59-61). Both defined config.py:250 (=25) and config.py:252 (=1200) and both actually break the loop. Two independent enforced caps.
spec_features.notes: max_iterations overridable via CLI (cli.py:49-50); max_wall_clock_s only via config but still enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py: 'max_iterations: int = 25  # max assistant turns before we stop the episode' ; 'max_wall_clock_s: int = 1200  # hard ceiling per episode'

code_only_features.evidence: Sandbox.run_tests runs the test command via subprocess with task.test_timeout_s (config.py:166 default 30); render() handles timed_out (sandbox.py:44-45). Bounds how long a single test run can hang.
code_only_features.justification_quote: sandbox docstring: 'executes whatever the model wrote, via ``subprocess`` with a timeout' (host-safety / hang prevention, not welfare)
